formula_references.jee_notes: Use net force, not an individual force.
Energy is scalar; speed is squared.
Force is a vector and follows inverse-square dependence.
Frequency controls photon energy; intensity controls photon number.

content.title: Projectile Range
content.summary: Horizontal range of a projectile landing at the same level from which it was projected.
content.explanation: Horizontal range of a projectile landing at the same level from which it was projected.
content.when_to_use: Use for ideal projectile motion with equal launch and landing levels.
assumptions: Launch and landing heights are equal.

example.question: For u=10 m/s, θ=45°, g=10 m/s².

common_mistakes: Using this formula for unequal heights.

content.title: Centripetal Acceleration
content.summary: Radial acceleration required for circular motion.
content.explanation: Radial acceleration required for circular motion.
conditions: Velocity direction changes even at constant speed.
assumptions: Motion is along a circle of radius r.
common_mistakes: Calling centripetal acceleration tangential.

content.title: Orbital Velocity
content.summary: Speed of a circular satellite orbit around a central mass.
content.explanation: Speed of a circular satellite orbit around a central mass.
conditions: Orbit is circular and gravitational force supplies centripetal force.

example.question: How does orbital speed change if r increases fourfold?

content.title: JEE Main Units and Measurements Quick Revision
content.summary: Five-to-ten minute revision note.

sections.heading: Must revise
points: Recall core equations and units.
Check vectors, signs, assumptions and limiting cases.
Interpret graphs and diagrams physically.
Audit units before accepting a numerical answer.

must_remember: Use SI units unless conversion is explicit.
common_mistakes: Using a formula outside its conditions.

content.title: Friction Direction
content.why_wrong: Friction opposes relative or impending relative motion, not necessarily the centre-of-mass velocity.
content.correct_approach: Determine the relative tendency at the contact and draw the free-body diagram.

content.title: Zero Potential Means Zero Field
content.why_wrong: Potential is scalar while field is the negative gradient of potential.
content.correct_approach: Check spatial variation of V; zero potential at one point does not imply zero field.

content.title: RMS Equals Peak
content.wrong_approach: Use peak AC value as RMS value.
content.why_wrong: For sinusoidal AC, RMS is peak divided by √2.
content.correct_approach: Identify whether the problem gives peak or RMS quantities.

content.title: Maximum Projectile Range
content.shortcut: For equal launch and landing levels, maximum range occurs at θ=45° and Rmax=u²/g.
content.example: For u=20 m/s,g=10 m/s², Rmax=40 m.

content.title: Velocity-Time Graph
content.relationship: Slope gives acceleration; area gives displacement.
interpretation: Read slope and area according to axis definitions.

content.title: Ohmic V-I Graph
content.relationship: Straight line through origin for constant resistance.
interpretation: Read slope and area according to axis definitions.

content.title: Photoelectric Effect Graph
content.relationship: Above threshold, maximum kinetic energy increases linearly with frequency.
interpretation: Read slope and area according to axis definitions.
